correctness.rationale: On S={x:1^Tx=0}, each Q_a is invertible. Splitting p_a=(pi_a+u_a)/2, using Q_0u_0=-Q_1u_1=z, yields (I+rH)z=-r(pi_1-pi_0) with H=-Q_0^-1-Q_1^-1; detailed balance annihilates each phase equilibrium flux. Hence J_e=-r L_e adj(I+rH)delta/[2 det(I+rH)], giving numerator degree <=dim S−1=n−2. H is invertible because Q0+Q1 irreducible on S. det stays positive for r>0 by uniqueness of the full irreducible switched chain and det(0)=1. Independent exact rational 6x6 stationary solution reproduces J=3r(8r−9)/(2(845r²+2559r+1530)) and root 9/8. All-n proof is resolvent algebra, not finite simulation.
residual_risks: The global ceiling counts positive rate zeros/multiplicity, not necessarily attainable reversals for n>3.

evidence: No-pumping theorems constrain cycles with fixed barrier or well data; six-state thermal engines are model-specific.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Those theorems do not imply the full arbitrary two-phase reversible-generator n−2 ceiling, and no-pumping hypotheses do not apply to the example because both conductances and weights vary.

originality.rationale: The exact n−2 numerator-degree ceiling for a single site-independent switching rate between two arbitrary separately reversible finite CTMC generators and its sharp three-site example is not among the inspected discrete-time ratchet, particular six-state engine, or no-pumping theorems. The matrix determinant/adjugate argument could have an unlocated general network-response antecedent.
residual_risks: General finite-state rational-resolvent response literature could imply the polynomial bound even without identical flashing-ratchet language.
The n−2 bound is constructively sharp for n=3 only; no all-n attainability claim.

This is substantive beyond generic rational dependence or a simple negative test.
residual_risks: No claims for nonreversible individual phases, nonsymmetric switching, or infinitely many sites.
